chunk_findings.detail: The new implementation assumes both `cfg.enforce` and `cfg.enforce.machine_local_keys` are present and iterable. The previous code deliberately treated a missing `enforce` section or a `machine_local_keys` value of `None` as “no extra keys” by returning `set()`. For a config-like object where `[enforce]` is absent or represented as `None` (for example a partially constructed config or a test double such as `types.SimpleNamespace(enforce=None)`), `_extra_keys` now raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'machine_local_keys'` instead of returning an empty set; if `machine_local_keys` itself is `None`, it raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. This can crash config/setup paths that previously handled missing optional enforce settings gracefully.

chunk_findings.detail: `_table_task` indexes `tbl` with the header column indices without checking that the data row actually has that many cells. A valid GFM table may omit trailing empty cells, so for header `| id | title | needs | globs |` and data row `| T-1 | Foo | Bar |` (missing the globs cell), `_table_cells` returns only three cells while `table_cols["globs"]` is `3`, causing an `IndexError` during import. The same applies to a row missing a `needs` cell.

chunk_findings.detail: `_table_row` treats any table-like row containing an exact `id` or `title` cell as a new header row, not as data. For example, after header `| id | title |`, a data row `| T-1 | id |` is classified as a header with `{"id": 1}`; the row is not imported, and subsequent rows are parsed with the wrong column mapping, silently dropping tasks.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new header promotion still promotes a table-like data row to a header whenever it contains a cell named `id` or `title` and the next line is delimiter-like, even when the scanner is already inside a table. Given:

```markdown
| id | title |
| --- | --- |
| T-1 | id |
| --- | --- |
| T-2 | Bar |
```

the second `| --- | --- |` is a data row of the first table under GFM (a visual separator), but at `| T-1 | id |` `_table_columns` yields a mapping containing `id`, `_table_delim` accepts the next line, and the scanner replaces the real column map with `{"id": 1}` and skips the separator. The task `T-1` is not emitted, and `T-2` is then parsed with the wrong column map (no title column) and is also dropped. The previous fix only prevented the misclassification when no delimiter-like row follows; with a delimiter-like data row the scanner still silently loses tasks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_scan_task_tables

The refutation run: _table_columns('| T-1 | id |') yields {'id':1} only because the cell IS the word 'id' -- an input that names a column, not a task. Refuted: not a real task row.

chunk_findings.detail: `_table_row` treats any table-like row containing an exact `id` or `title` cell as a new header row, not as data. chunk_findings.detail:
The new header promotion still promotes a table-like data row to a header whenever it contains a cell named `id` or `title` and the next line is delimiter-like, even when the scanner is already inside a table. Given:

```markdown
| id | title |
| --- | --- |
| T-1 | id |
| --- | --- |
| T-2 | Bar |
```

the second `| --- | --- |` is a data row of the first table under GFM (a visual separator), but at `| T-1 | id |` `_table_columns` yields a mapping containing `id`, `_table_delim` accepts the next line, and the scanner replaces the real column map with `{"id": 1}` and skips the separator. The task `T-1` is not emitted, and `T-2` is then parsed with the wrong column map (no title column) and is also dropped. The previous fix only prevented the misclassification when no delimiter-like row follows; with a delimiter-like data row the scanner still silently loses tasks.

chunk_findings.detail: The exception path is not atomic: `bug.repro_runs = int(sig.get("runs") or 0)` is assigned before `bug.repro_failures` is converted. Given a persisted sighting whose `runs` is valid but whose `failures` is malformed, e.g. `sighted={"reproduced":"yes","runs":1,"failures":"boom"}` on a record where `bug.repro_failures` is already `5`, `_merge_sighted` sets `bug.repro_runs = 1`, then the `int("boom")` raises and is swallowed. The except comment says a persisted sighting whose counts cannot count "folds nothing", but the run count and `reproduced` flag have already been folded, leaving the impossible state `runs=1, failures=5` (e.g. a 500% failure rate) instead of leaving the old counts untouched.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/knowledge.py:_merge_sighted

chunk_findings.detail: The gate `if not b.open or (b.reproduced != "yes" and b.sightings < SIGHTINGS_THAT_CONFIRM): continue` treats `reproduced == ""` ("none": no repro command has run) the same as `reproduced == "no"` (a repro command ran and exited 0). A `bug found` invocation that does not pass the new `--repro-cmd` — which is still the pre-existing filing path described in the change — leaves `reproduced` as the default `""` while `sightings` is only 1, so its `item`/`fix_task` is removed from the priority ID set even though this change’s own docstring says only “its repro command ran and did not fail” is unconfirmed. Existing open bugs loaded from old records have the same defaults (`reproduced=""`, `sightings=0`) and silently stop being offered. If the intent is to demote demonstrated non-failing runs only, gate on `b.reproduced == "no"` (or migrate legacy records to count as the first sighting).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:727

chunk_findings.detail: The function returns `(F.tree(repo) or {}).get("tree_sha", "")`, but the default `""` only applies when the `"tree_sha"` key is missing, not when it is present with value `None`. If `F.tree(repo)` produces `{"tree_sha": None}` (for example, a repository whose tree info has no sha), this returns `None` despite the `-> str` annotation and the docstring’s promise that unreadable trees degrade to an empty sha. `RC.check` then receives `None` instead of `""`, so the “check answers 'unavailable' to an empty sha” path is bypassed, which can crash or misclassify the run during `bug found --repro-cmd`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprobundle.py:_tree_sha_safely

chunk_findings.detail:
When `given["check"]` is supplied, `attach` takes `run = given.get("check")`, so the pre-run
snapshot block is skipped and `events`/`machine` are first read in the inner `try`, after the
caller's check has already executed the repro command. The bundle then stores machine load
and log entries as if they were the pre-run snapshot, even though they were captured after
the command ran. Example: a caller runs `run = RC.check(repo, sha, "pytest ...", ...)` and
then calls `attach(..., check=run)`; `F.machine(repo)` is invoked after pytest has finished,
so the recorded load is not the bug-time/load condition needed for flaky-repro evidence.
Either the pre-run reads must happen before a caller-supplied check, or the caller-supplied
check must carry its own pre-run machine/events with it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprobundle.py:attach

chunk_findings.detail: `W.scratch_tree` is the regression-verify worktree code (`services/gates/mutation.py`), and with `detach=True` it creates a linked git worktree. In a linked worktree, `.git` is a regular file, not a directory, so `(s.path / ".git" / "config").read_bytes()` raises `OSError` before any command runs, and `_run_at` returns `{"unavailable": "the scratch checkout's .git/config is not readable"}`. The normal `bug found --repro-cmd ...` path therefore never executes the repro command, defeating the feature. The code's own comment names linked worktrees but treats the standard scratch worktree path as unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_run_at

chunk_findings.detail: `_one_run` discards any run whose final shell exit status is 126 or 127. POSIX uses those statuses when the shell cannot execute a command, but an executed program may also legitimately exit 126 or 127. Given `line = "python -c 'import sys; sys.exit(127)'"`, the outer shell executes `python` and exits with 127; `_one_run` returns `None`, the run is counted as unreached, and `check` reports `unavailable` instead of `reproduced: "yes"`. This contradicts the module’s stated contract that a reproduction is any run that exited non-zero.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_one_run

chunk_findings.detail: The new comment promises “Both counts count or NEITHER folds”, but the code still folds `repro_runs` when the sighting supplies a run count but no failure count. Given a persisted sighting such as `{"runs": 1}` (or `{"runs": 0}`) on a bug whose stored `repro_failures` is already `5`, `sig.get("failures") is not None` is false, so `new_failures` remains `None`; the `else` block then assigns `bug.repro_runs = 1` while leaving `bug.repro_failures = 5`. The record now has more failures than runs (or zero runs with failures), so any failure-rate computation from these stored counts is wrong (e.g. 500%, or division by zero for `runs=0`). A sighting that cannot supply a failure count should fold nothing, as the comment says.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/knowledge.py:_merge_sighted

chunk_findings.detail: `_prime_scratch` now trusts whatever `git -C scratch rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` returns and then runs `git clean`/`git reset` against that resolved gitdir. A repro command can replace the linked worktree’s `.git` pointer (for example `echo "gitdir: [REDACTED:path]" > .git`) and exit with a failure; on the next run of a multi-run repro, `_git_dir` follows the poisoned pointer, `_prime_scratch` deletes `HEAD.lock`/`index.lock` in the external repository, and the subsequent `git clean -xdfq -f` and `git reset --hard <sha>` operate through that external gitdir (moving/corrupting its HEAD/index, and its worktree if `core.worktree` is set) while `_prime_scratch` returns `True` as if the scratch had been reset. The previous code refused when `.git` was a symlink; the new code has no check that the resolved gitdir is the scratch’s own worktree metadata.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_prime_scratch

chunk_findings.detail: The new table scanner is dead code in the shipped importer. The importer.py diff is `+116 -0` and contains only the definitions `_table_cells`, `_table_columns`, `_table_delim`, `_col`, `_table_task`, and `_scan_task_tables`; no added line calls `_scan_task_tables` from `scan_todos` or any other import path. Therefore a markdown file containing the reported task table is still parsed by the old code, and SX-seed’s title remains cut at the pipe. A test that calls `_scan_task_tables` directly can pass while the user-visible bug is unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_scan_task_tables

chunk_findings.detail:
`_table_delim` returns `True` for an empty row because `_table_cells('')` returns `['']` and the `all()` accepts `c.strip() == ""`. `_scan_task_tables` uses it as the GFM delimiter test and does not require `lines[i + 1]` to be a nonblank table row. Given:

```markdown
| id | title |

| X | Task |
```

line 0 activates `cols`, the blank line is consumed as the delimiter, and line 2 is parsed as a task row (`id="X"`, `title="Task"`). A blank line should terminate a GFM table; this imports tasks from unrelated pipe lines separated by blank lines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_table_delim

chunk_findings.detail: The split regex `(?<!\\)\|` treats any pipe preceded by one backslash as escaped, even when that backslash is itself escaped. In a GFM row `` `| a\\|b |` `` (two backslashes before the pipe), the `\\` is a literal backslash and the following `|` is a column separator, so the row should produce cells `a\` and `b`. `_table_cells` does not split there and returns a merged cell (effectively `a\|b`), which shifts the `needs`/`globs` columns in `_table_task`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_table_cells
